exposure: Trauma-informed support programme based on psychological first aid (PFA)
cohort: The study included 101 women aged 18 or older who had experienced a complicated childbirth, defined by conditions such as acute/emergency caesarean section, vacuum extraction, or major haemorrhage.
finding: The trauma-informed support program significantly reduced post-traumatic stress symptoms in women after a complicated childbirth, but showed no significant effect on fear of childbirth, depression, or anxiety.
